findings.title: Model-controlled tool argument reaches a dangerous sink
findings.description: Tool `network_check` passes a model-controlled argument to `subprocess.run` (command execution). A prompt-injected model chooses this value. The data passes through `run_network_check()` parameter `host` and reaches the sink at app/system_utils.py:12.
findings.recommendation: Validate tool arguments against a strict schema and allow-list. Use parameterized queries, argument arrays without a shell, and path/URL allow-lists.

findings.title: Indirect prompt injection: external content reaches an agent with privileged tools
findings.description: Untrusted external content (`WebBaseLoader`) can reach agent context while the agent can call side-effecting tools (`ShellTool`, `lookup_customer`, `network_check`). Instructions hidden in fetched content can trigger those tools.
findings.recommendation: Treat retrieved and fetched content as data: isolate it from tool-calling agents, restrict tools to least privilege, and require human approval for side effects.

findings.title: Credential embedded in a system prompt
findings.description: The system prompt text appears to contain a credential.
findings.recommendation: Assume system prompts can be extracted. Remove credentials and sensitive rules from prompts and enforce authorization outside the model.

findings.title: Tool takes an object or identity reference from the model (confused deputy)
findings.description: Tool `lookup_customer` lets the model choose `customer_id` and receives no caller identity (no InjectedToolArg/InjectedState/config). A prompt-injected model can act on other users' records with the agent's privileges (IDOR / confused deputy).
findings.recommendation: Inject the caller's identity into the tool (InjectedToolArg, InjectedState, or the RunnableConfig) and authorize every object access against it; never trust IDs chosen by the model.

findings.title: No human approval before side-effecting tool calls
findings.description: Side-effecting tools (`ShellTool`, `lookup_customer`, `network_check`) run without any detected human approval step (no LangGraph interrupt, interrupt_before/after, or human-in-the-loop middleware).
findings.recommendation: Use LangGraph interrupts (interrupt_before / interrupt()) or human-in-the-loop middleware so a person approves destructive or external actions.

findings.title: LLM entry point has no detected authentication
findings.description: `POST /chat` exposes LLM functionality without detected authentication; anyone who can reach it can spend model quota and drive connected tools.
findings.recommendation: Require authentication and authorization on the endpoint, and add rate limits and usage quotas to protect model spend and connected tools.

findings.title: Secret or personal data sent to a model
findings.description: Personal data is sent to the model via .invoke().
findings.recommendation: Minimize and redact data before prompting. Confirm the provider's retention terms and keep credentials out of prompts entirely.

findings.title: Untrusted input concatenated into a prompt
findings.description: User input is formatted directly into .invoke(); it is not delimited from instructions and braces in the input can inject template variables.
findings.recommendation: Pass user input as a separate template variable or human message; never splice it into instructions. Delimit untrusted text and validate its length and format.
